subtitle: How a Democratic Congress should use the majority voters gave it
description: A position paper, resolution, and source notes from the Andover Democratic Town Committee on how the new congressional majority should use its power.

cards.essay: The argument in about a thousand words: accept the power, use it with discipline, and spend it on the work that matters most.
cards.resolution: The same position in Whereas and Resolved form, written so that another committee can amend it line by line and adopt it.
cards.notes: The basis for each factual claim, with the caveats the essay compresses, and further reading on the wider debate, including the arguments the essay answers.

intro: The November 2026 elections gave Democrats control of both chambers of Congress, and advice about what to do with that power arrived from every direction. Some urged the new majority to do as little as possible beyond the cost of living. Others urged it to do everything at once.

This paper argues for a third course: accept the power and use it with discipline. The test for every hearing, subpoena, and bill should be how much it matters, not how many wins it produces or how easily they come. The paper names where that work should begin, and it ends on the reason for doing it at all, which is to restore a government of the people, by the people, and for the people.
sources: The essay and the resolution make an argument and leave their sources out. The notes supply them. Every source cited there also has a short, stable page on this site, and the full set is collected at [docs.andoverctdems.com/links/301](/links/301/).
committees: We invite our fellow Democratic committees to amend this paper and adopt it. The Word versions are provided for that purpose. In the resolution, substitute your committee's name in the first Resolved clause.
